newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to seek G7 funds for Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to seek G7 funds for Jordan.

text.p: President Bill Clinton met with Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan on Wednesday and said he planned to ask the summit of the seven industrial nations meeting in Denver to contribute to a Mideast stability fund.
The United States announced on Tuesday it was taking $100 million out of this year's aid to Israel and Egypt, and giving it to Jordan to reward Amman for its dedication to Middle East peace efforts.
The aid will be channelled to Jordan through a newly-created Middle East peace and stability fund.

White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry said in a statement that Clinton and Hassan discussed the fund. He said its "initial focus will be on assisting Jordan as it persues economic modernisation and reform."
"The president said he would encourage his colleagues at the Denver summit to make similar contributions to encourage peace and stability in the region," McCurry said.
The economic summit, which begins on Friday, will be attended by the leaders of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy and Japan. Russian President Boris Yeltsin also will participate.
After the White House meeting, Hassan told reporters Jordan was grateful for the U.S. assistance and pledged to continue working for peace in the region.
"We are not going to give up," Hassan said of efforts to ease tensions. "There's no question of our not persevering in attempting to build peace."
"Clearly we have to find ways and means of making this thing work, and that's what we're applying ourselves to," he said.
